stem: Write an anti derivative for each of the following functions using the method of inspection: (i) \(\cos 2x\)  (ii) \(3x^2 + 4x^3\)  (iii) \(\dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x \neq 0\).
solution:
(i) We look for a function whose derivative is \(\cos 2x\). Since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\sin 2x = 2\cos 2x\), we have \(\cos 2x = \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin 2x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x\right)\). Therefore an anti derivative of \(\cos 2x\) is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\sin 2x\).
(ii) Note that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^3 + x^4\right) = 3x^2 + 4x^3\). Therefore an anti derivative of \(3x^2 + 4x^3\) is \(x^3 + x^4\).
(iii) We know that \(\dfrac{d}{dx}(\log x) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x > 0\) and \(\dfrac{d}{dx}[\log(-x)] = \dfrac{1}{-x}(-1) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x < 0\). Combining these, \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\log|x|\right) = \dfrac{1}{x}\), \(x \neq 0\). Therefore \(\int \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \log|x|\) is one of the anti derivatives of \(\dfrac{1}{x}\).

stem: Find the following integrals: (i) \(\int \dfrac{x^3 - 1}{x^2}\,dx\)  (ii) \(\int \left(x^{2/3} + 1\right) dx\)  (iii) \(\int \left(x^{3/2} + 2e^x - \dfrac{1}{x}\right) dx\).

(i) \(\int \dfrac{x^3 - 1}{x^2}\,dx = \int x\,dx - \int x^{-2}\,dx\) (by Property V) \(= \dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{x^{-1}}{-1} + C = \dfrac{x^2}{2} + \dfrac{1}{x} + C\), where \(C\) is a constant of integration.
(ii) \(\int \left(x^{2/3} + 1\right) dx = \int x^{2/3}\,dx + \int dx = \dfrac{x^{2/3 + 1}}{\tfrac{2}{3} + 1} + x + C = \dfrac{3}{5}x^{5/3} + x + C\).
(iii) \(\int \left(x^{3/2} + 2e^x - \dfrac{1}{x}\right) dx = \int x^{3/2}\,dx + \int 2e^x\,dx - \int \dfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \dfrac{x^{3/2 + 1}}{\tfrac{3}{2} + 1} + 2e^x - \log|x| + C = \dfrac{2}{5}x^{5/2} + 2e^x - \log|x| + C\).

stem: Find the following integrals: (i) \(\int (\sin x + \cos x)\,dx\)  (ii) \(\int \csc x\,(\csc x + \cot x)\,dx\)  (iii) \(\int \dfrac{1 - \sin x}{\cos^2 x}\,dx\).
solution:
(i) \(\int (\sin x + \cos x)\,dx = \int \sin x\,dx + \int \cos x\,dx = -\cos x + \sin x + C\).
(ii) \(\int \csc x\,(\csc x + \cot x)\,dx = \int \csc^2 x\,dx + \int \csc x \cot x\,dx = -\cot x - \csc x + C\).
(iii) \(\int \dfrac{1 - \sin x}{\cos^2 x}\,dx = \int \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 x}\,dx - \int \dfrac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x}\,dx = \int \sec^2 x\,dx - \int \tan x \sec x\,dx = \tan x - \sec x + C\).

stem: Find the anti derivative \(F\) of \(f\) defined by \(f(x) = 4x^3 - 6\), where \(F(0) = 3\).
solution: One anti derivative of \(f(x)\) is \(x^4 - 6x\), since \(\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(x^4 - 6x\right) = 4x^3 - 6\). Therefore the anti derivative \(F\) is given by \(F(x) = x^4 - 6x + C\), where \(C\) is a constant. Given \(F(0) = 3\), which gives \(3 = 0 - 6 \times 0 + C\), or \(C = 3\). solution: Let \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^2 x\,dx\). By \(\int_{0}^{a} f(x)\,dx = \int_{0}^{a} f(a-x)\,dx\), \(I = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \cos^2\!\left(\tfrac{\pi}{2}-x\right)dx = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \sin^2 x\,dx\). Derivative of \(\tan^{-1} x\) is \(\frac{1}{1 + x^2}\). Thus, we use the substitution \(\tan^{-1} x = t\) so that \(\frac{dx}{1 + x^2} = dt\). Therefore, \(\int \frac{\sin (\tan^{-1} x)}{1 + x^2}\,dx = \int \sin t\,dt = -\cos t + C = -\cos (\tan^{-1} x) + C\).

We have \(\int \sin^3 x \cos^2 x\,dx = \int \sin^2 x \cos^2 x (\sin x)\,dx = \int (1 - \cos^2 x)\cos^2 x (\sin x)\,dx\). Put \(t = \cos x\) so that \(dt = -\sin x\,dx\). Therefore, \(\int \sin^2 x \cos^2 x (\sin x)\,dx = -\int (1 - t^2) t^2\,dt = -\int (t^2 - t^4)\,dt = -\left(\frac{t^3}{3} - \frac{t^5}{5}\right) + C = -\frac{1}{3}\cos^3 x + \frac{1}{5}\cos^5 x + C\).

Put \(x + a = t\). Then \(dx = dt\). Therefore, \(\int \frac{\sin x}{\sin (x + a)}\,dx = \int \frac{\sin (t - a)}{\sin t}\,dt = \int \frac{\sin t \cos a - \cos t \sin a}{\sin t}\,dt = \cos a \int dt - \sin a \int \cot t\,dt = (\cos a)\,t - (\sin a)\left[\log |\sin t| + C_1\right] = (\cos a)(x + a) - (\sin a)\left[\log |\sin (x + a)| + C_1\right] = x \cos a + a \cos a - (\sin a)\log |\sin (x + a)| - C_1 \sin a\). Hence, \(\int \frac{\sin x}{\sin (x + a)}\,dx = x \cos a - \sin a \log |\sin (x + a)| + C\), where \(C = -C_1 \sin a + a \cos a\), is another arbitrary constant.

\(\int \frac{dx}{1 + \tan x} = \int \frac{\cos x\,dx}{\cos x + \sin x} = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{(\cos x + \sin x + \cos x - \sin x)\,dx}{\cos x + \sin x} = \frac{1}{2}\int dx + \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{C_1}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx\) ...(1). Now, consider \(I = \int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx\). Put \(\cos x + \sin x = t\) so that \((\cos x - \sin x)\,dx = dt\). Therefore \(I = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log |t| + C_2 = \log |\cos x + \sin x| + C_2\). Putting it in (1), we get \(\int \frac{dx}{1 + \tan x} = \frac{x}{2} + \frac{1}{2}\log |\cos x + \sin x| + C\), where \(C = \frac{C_1}{2} + \frac{C_2}{2}\).
Put \(t = 1 + x^2\), so \(dt = 2x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{2x}{1 + x^2}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log|t| + C = \log(1 + x^2) + C\).
Put \(t = \log x\), so \(dt = \tfrac{1}{x}\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{(\log x)^2}{x}\,dx = \int t^2\,dt = \frac{t^3}{3} + C = \frac{(\log x)^3}{3} + C\).
Write \(x + x\log x = x(1 + \log x)\). Put \(t = 1 + \log x\), so \(dt = \tfrac{1}{x}\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{1}{x(1 + \log x)}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log|t| + C = \log|1 + \log x| + C\).
Put \(t = \cos x\), so \(dt = -\sin x\,dx\). Then \(\int \sin x\,\sin(\cos x)\,dx = -\int \sin t\,dt = \cos t + C = \cos(\cos x) + C\).
Put \(t = \sin(ax + b)\), so \(dt = a\cos(ax + b)\,dx\). Then \(\int \sin(ax + b)\cos(ax + b)\,dx = \frac{1}{a}\int t\,dt = \frac{t^2}{2a} + C = \frac{\sin^2(ax + b)}{2a} + C\).
Put \(t = ax + b\), so \(dt = a\,dx\). Then \(\int \sqrt{ax + b}\,dx = \frac{1}{a}\int t^{1/2}\,dt = \frac{1}{a}\cdot\frac{2}{3}t^{3/2} + C = \frac{2}{3a}(ax + b)^{3/2} + C\).

Put \(t = \sqrt{x}\), so \(x = t^2\) and \(dx = 2t\,dt\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{x - \sqrt{x}} = \int \frac{2t\,dt}{t^2 - t} = \int \frac{2t\,dt}{t(t - 1)} = \int \frac{2}{t - 1}\,dt = 2\log|t - 1| + C = 2\log|\sqrt{x} - 1| + C\).

stem: Integrate the function \(\dfrac{1}{x (\log x)^m},\ x > 0,\ m \ne 1\).
solution: Put \(t = \log x\), so \(dt = \tfrac{1}{x}\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{x(\log x)^m} = \int t^{-m}\,dt = \frac{t^{1 - m}}{1 - m} + C = \frac{(\log x)^{1 - m}}{1 - m} + C\) (for \(m \ne 1\)).
Put \(t = 9 - 4x^2\), so \(dt = -8x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{x}{9 - 4x^2}\,dx = -\frac{1}{8}\int \frac{dt}{t} = -\frac{1}{8}\log|t| + C = -\frac{1}{8}\log|9 - 4x^2| + C\).
Put \(t = 2x + 3\), so \(dt = 2\,dx\). Then \(\int e^{2x + 3}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int e^t\,dt = \frac{1}{2}e^{2x + 3} + C\).

The integrand is \(x e^{-x^2}\). Put \(t = x^2\), so \(dt = 2x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{x}{e^{x^2}}\,dx = \int x e^{-x^2}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int e^{-t}\,dt = -\frac{1}{2}e^{-t} + C = -\frac{1}{2}e^{-x^2} + C\).
Put \(t = \tan^{-1} x\), so \(dt = \frac{dx}{1 + x^2}\). Then \(\int \frac{e^{\tan^{-1} x}}{1 + x^2}\,dx = \int e^t\,dt = e^t + C = e^{\tan^{-1} x} + C\).

Divide numerator and denominator by \(e^x\): \(\frac{e^{2x} - 1}{e^{2x} + 1} = \frac{e^x - e^{-x}}{e^x + e^{-x}}\). Put \(t = e^x + e^{-x}\), so \(dt = (e^x - e^{-x})\,dx\). Then the integral \(= \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log|t| + C = \log(e^x + e^{-x}) + C\).
Use \(\tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta - 1\): \(\int \tan^2(2x - 3)\,dx = \int \left(\sec^2(2x - 3) - 1\right)dx = \frac{1}{2}\tan(2x - 3) - x + C\).
Put \(t = 7 - 4x\), so \(dt = -4\,dx\). Then \(\int \sec^2(7 - 4x)\,dx = -\frac{1}{4}\int \sec^2 t\,dt = -\frac{1}{4}\tan t + C = -\frac{1}{4}\tan(7 - 4x) + C\).
Put \(t = \sin^{-1} x\), so \(dt = \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\). Then \(\int \frac{\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}\,dx = \int t\,dt = \frac{t^2}{2} + C = \frac{(\sin^{-1} x)^2}{2} + C\).

stem: Integrate the function \(\dfrac{2 \cos x - 3 \sin x}{6 \cos x + 4 \sin x}\).
solution: Observe \(\frac{d}{dx}(6\cos x + 4\sin x) = -6\sin x + 4\cos x = 2(2\cos x - 3\sin x)\). Put \(t = 6\cos x + 4\sin x\), so \(dt = 2(2\cos x - 3\sin x)\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{2\cos x - 3\sin x}{6\cos x + 4\sin x}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{t} = \frac{1}{2}\log|t| + C = \frac{1}{2}\log|6\cos x + 4\sin x| + C\).

Write \(\frac{1}{\cos^2 x(1 - \tan x)^2} = \frac{\sec^2 x}{(1 - \tan x)^2}\). Put \(t = 1 - \tan x\), so \(dt = -\sec^2 x\,dx\). Then the integral \(= -\int \frac{dt}{t^2} = \frac{1}{t} + C = \frac{1}{1 - \tan x} + C\).
Put \(t = \sqrt{x}\), so \(dt = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{x}}\,dx\), i.e. \(\frac{dx}{\sqrt{x}} = 2\,dt\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos\sqrt{x}}{\sqrt{x}}\,dx = 2\int \cos t\,dt = 2\sin t + C = 2\sin\sqrt{x} + C\).
Put \(t = \sin 2x\), so \(dt = 2\cos 2x\,dx\). Then \(\int \sqrt{\sin 2x}\,\cos 2x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int t^{1/2}\,dt = \frac{1}{2}\cdot\frac{2}{3}t^{3/2} + C = \frac{1}{3}(\sin 2x)^{3/2} + C\).
Put \(t = 1 + \sin x\), so \(dt = \cos x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x}{\sqrt{1 + \sin x}}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t}} = 2\sqrt{t} + C = 2\sqrt{1 + \sin x} + C\).
Put \(t = \log\sin x\), so \(dt = \frac{\cos x}{\sin x}\,dx = \cot x\,dx\). Then \(\int \cot x\,\log\sin x\,dx = \int t\,dt = \frac{t^2}{2} + C = \frac{(\log\sin x)^2}{2} + C\).
Put \(t = 1 + \cos x\), so \(dt = -\sin x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\sin x}{1 + \cos x}\,dx = -\int \frac{dt}{t} = -\log|t| + C = -\log|1 + \cos x| + C\).
Put \(t = 1 + \cos x\), so \(dt = -\sin x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\sin x}{(1 + \cos x)^2}\,dx = -\int \frac{dt}{t^2} = \frac{1}{t} + C = \frac{1}{1 + \cos x} + C\).

\(\frac{1}{1 + \cot x} = \frac{\sin x}{\sin x + \cos x}\). Let \(I = \int \frac{\sin x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx\) and \(J = \int \frac{\cos x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx\). Then \(I + J = \int 1\,dx = x\) and \(J - I = \int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\sin x + \cos x}\,dx = \log|\sin x + \cos x|\). Subtracting, \(2I = x - \log|\sin x + \cos x|\), so \(I = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \log|\sin x + \cos x|\right) + C\).

\(\frac{1}{1 - \tan x} = \frac{\cos x}{\cos x - \sin x}\). Let \(I = \int \frac{\cos x}{\cos x - \sin x}\,dx\) and \(J = \int \frac{\sin x}{\cos x - \sin x}\,dx\). Then \(I - J = \int 1\,dx = x\) and \(I + J = \int \frac{\cos x + \sin x}{\cos x - \sin x}\,dx = -\log|\cos x - \sin x|\) (since \(\frac{d}{dx}(\cos x - \sin x) = -(\cos x + \sin x)\)). Adding, \(2I = x - \log|\cos x - \sin x|\), so \(I = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \log|\cos x - \sin x|\right) + C\).

stem: Integrate the function \(\dfrac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{\sin x \cos x}\).
solution: Write \(\sin x\cos x = \cos^2 x\,\tan x\), so \(\frac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{\sin x\cos x} = \frac{\sqrt{\tan x}}{\cos^2 x\,\tan x} = \frac{\sec^2 x}{\sqrt{\tan x}}\). Put \(t = \tan x\), so \(dt = \sec^2 x\,dx\). Then the integral \(= \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t}} = 2\sqrt{t} + C = 2\sqrt{\tan x} + C\).
Put \(t = 1 + \log x\), so \(dt = \tfrac{1}{x}\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{(1 + \log x)^2}{x}\,dx = \int t^2\,dt = \frac{t^3}{3} + C = \frac{(1 + \log x)^3}{3} + C\).

Write \(\frac{(x + 1)(x + \log x)^2}{x} = (x + \log x)^2\left(1 + \frac{1}{x}\right)\). Put \(t = x + \log x\), so \(dt = \left(1 + \frac{1}{x}\right)dx\). Then the integral \(= \int t^2\,dt = \frac{t^3}{3} + C = \frac{(x + \log x)^3}{3} + C\).

Put \(t = \tan^{-1}(x^4)\), so \(dt = \frac{4x^3}{1 + x^8}\,dx\), i.e. \(\frac{x^3}{1 + x^8}\,dx = \frac{dt}{4}\). Then \(\int \frac{x^3\sin(\tan^{-1} x^4)}{1 + x^8}\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\int \sin t\,dt = -\frac{1}{4}\cos t + C = -\frac{1}{4}\cos(\tan^{-1} x^4) + C\).

Recall the identity \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1\), which gives \(\cos^2 x = \dfrac{1+\cos 2x}{2}\). Therefore \(\int \cos^2 x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int (1+\cos 2x)\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\int dx + \dfrac{1}{2}\int \cos 2x\,dx = \dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4}\sin 2x + C\).

Recall the identity \(\sin x \cos y = \dfrac{1}{2}[\sin (x+y) + \sin (x-y)]\). Then \(\int \sin 2x \cos 3x\,dx = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[\int \sin 5x\,dx - \int \sin x\,dx\right] = \dfrac{1}{2}\left[-\dfrac{1}{5}\cos 5x + \cos x\right] + C = -\dfrac{1}{10}\cos 5x + \dfrac{1}{2}\cos x + C\).

From the identity \(\sin 3x = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x\), we find that \(\sin^3 x = \dfrac{3\sin x - \sin 3x}{4}\). Therefore \(\int \sin^3 x\,dx = \dfrac{3}{4}\int \sin x\,dx - \dfrac{1}{4}\int \sin 3x\,dx = -\dfrac{3}{4}\cos x + \dfrac{1}{12}\cos 3x + C\). Alternatively, \(\int \sin^3 x\,dx = \int (1-\cos^2 x)\sin x\,dx\); putting \(\cos x = t\) so that \(-\sin x\,dx = dt\) gives \(-\int (1-t^2)\,dt = -t + \dfrac{t^3}{3} + C = -\cos x + \dfrac{1}{3}\cos^3 x + C\). Both answers are equivalent.

Use the power-reduction identity \(\sin^2\theta = \frac{1 - \cos 2\theta}{2}\) with \(\theta = 2x+5\): \(\sin^2(2x+5) = \frac{1 - \cos(4x+10)}{2}\). Then \(\int \sin^2(2x+5)\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int \left(1 - \cos(4x+10)\right)dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{\sin(4x+10)}{4}\right) + C = \frac{x}{2} - \frac{\sin(4x+10)}{8} + C\).

Use the product-to-sum identity \(\sin A \cos B = \frac{1}{2}\left[\sin(A+B) + \sin(A-B)\right]\): \(\sin 3x \cos 4x = \frac{1}{2}\left[\sin 7x + \sin(-x)\right] = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sin 7x - \sin x\right)\). Then \(\int \sin 3x \cos 4x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(-\frac{\cos 7x}{7} + \cos x\right) + C = -\frac{\cos 7x}{14} + \frac{\cos x}{2} + C\).

First \(\cos 2x \cos 4x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 6x + \cos 2x)\), so \(\cos 2x \cos 4x \cos 6x = \frac{1}{2}\cos 6x(\cos 6x + \cos 2x) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\cos^2 6x + \cos 2x \cos 6x\right)\). Using \(\cos^2 6x = \frac{1+\cos 12x}{2}\) and \(\cos 2x \cos 6x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 8x + \cos 4x)\), this becomes \(\frac{1}{4}\left(1 + \cos 4x + \cos 8x + \cos 12x\right)\). Then \(\int \cos 2x \cos 4x \cos 6x\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\left(x + \frac{\sin 4x}{4} + \frac{\sin 8x}{8} + \frac{\sin 12x}{12}\right) + C\).

Use \(\sin^3\theta = \frac{3\sin\theta - \sin 3\theta}{4}\) with \(\theta = 2x+1\): \(\sin^3(2x+1) = \frac{1}{4}\left[3\sin(2x+1) - \sin(6x+3)\right]\). Then \(\int \sin^3(2x+1)\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\left[-\frac{3\cos(2x+1)}{2} + \frac{\cos(6x+3)}{6}\right] + C = -\frac{3\cos(2x+1)}{8} + \frac{\cos(6x+3)}{24} + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\sin^3 x \cos^3 x\).
solution: Since \(\sin x \cos x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x\), \(\sin^3 x \cos^3 x = (\sin x \cos x)^3 = \frac{1}{8}\sin^3 2x\). Using \(\sin^3 2x = \frac{3\sin 2x - \sin 6x}{4}\), \(\int \sin^3 x \cos^3 x\,dx = \frac{1}{32}\int(3\sin 2x - \sin 6x)\,dx = \frac{1}{32}\left(-\frac{3\cos 2x}{2} + \frac{\cos 6x}{6}\right) + C = -\frac{3\cos 2x}{64} + \frac{\cos 6x}{192} + C\).

Pair \(\sin x \sin 3x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 2x - \cos 4x)\), so \(\sin x \sin 2x \sin 3x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 2x(\cos 2x - \cos 4x) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\sin 2x \cos 2x - \sin 2x \cos 4x\right)\). With \(\sin 2x \cos 2x = \frac{1}{2}\sin 4x\) and \(\sin 2x \cos 4x = \frac{1}{2}(\sin 6x - \sin 2x)\), this equals \(\frac{1}{4}(\sin 4x - \sin 6x + \sin 2x)\). Then \(\int \sin x \sin 2x \sin 3x\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\left(-\frac{\cos 4x}{4} + \frac{\cos 6x}{6} - \frac{\cos 2x}{2}\right) + C = \frac{\cos 6x}{24} - \frac{\cos 4x}{16} - \frac{\cos 2x}{8} + C\).

Use \(\sin A \sin B = \frac{1}{2}\left[\cos(A-B) - \cos(A+B)\right]\): \(\sin 4x \sin 8x = \frac{1}{2}(\cos 4x - \cos 12x)\). Then \(\int \sin 4x \sin 8x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{\sin 4x}{4} - \frac{\sin 12x}{12}\right) + C = \frac{\sin 4x}{8} - \frac{\sin 12x}{24} + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{1 - \cos x}{1 + \cos x}\).
solution: Using \(1 - \cos x = 2\sin^2\frac{x}{2}\) and \(1 + \cos x = 2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}\), \(\frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x} = \tan^2\frac{x}{2} = \sec^2\frac{x}{2} - 1\). Then \(\int \frac{1-\cos x}{1+\cos x}\,dx = \int\left(\sec^2\frac{x}{2} - 1\right)dx = 2\tan\frac{x}{2} - x + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{\cos x}{1 + \cos x}\).
solution: Write \(\frac{\cos x}{1+\cos x} = \frac{(1+\cos x) - 1}{1+\cos x} = 1 - \frac{1}{1+\cos x}\). Since \(1+\cos x = 2\cos^2\frac{x}{2}\), \(\frac{1}{1+\cos x} = \frac{1}{2}\sec^2\frac{x}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x}{1+\cos x}\,dx = \int\left(1 - \frac{1}{2}\sec^2\frac{x}{2}\right)dx = x - \tan\frac{x}{2} + C\).

\(\sin^4 x = \left(\frac{1-\cos 2x}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}\left(1 - 2\cos 2x + \cos^2 2x\right)\). Replacing \(\cos^2 2x = \frac{1+\cos 4x}{2}\) gives \(\sin^4 x = \frac{3}{8} - \frac{\cos 2x}{2} + \frac{\cos 4x}{8}\). Then \(\int \sin^4 x\,dx = \frac{3x}{8} - \frac{\sin 2x}{4} + \frac{\sin 4x}{32} + C\).

\(\cos^4 2x = \left(\frac{1+\cos 4x}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{1}{4}\left(1 + 2\cos 4x + \cos^2 4x\right)\). Using \(\cos^2 4x = \frac{1+\cos 8x}{2}\) gives \(\cos^4 2x = \frac{3}{8} + \frac{\cos 4x}{2} + \frac{\cos 8x}{8}\). Then \(\int \cos^4 2x\,dx = \frac{3x}{8} + \frac{\sin 4x}{8} + \frac{\sin 8x}{64} + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{\sin^2 x}{1 + \cos x}\).
solution: Since \(\sin^2 x = 1 - \cos^2 x = (1-\cos x)(1+\cos x)\), \(\frac{\sin^2 x}{1+\cos x} = 1 - \cos x\). Then \(\int \frac{\sin^2 x}{1+\cos x}\,dx = \int(1 - \cos x)\,dx = x - \sin x + C\).

Using \(\cos 2x = 2\cos^2 x - 1\) and \(\cos 2\alpha = 2\cos^2\alpha - 1\), the numerator \(\cos 2x - \cos 2\alpha = 2(\cos^2 x - \cos^2\alpha) = 2(\cos x - \cos\alpha)(\cos x + \cos\alpha)\). Hence \(\frac{\cos 2x - \cos 2\alpha}{\cos x - \cos\alpha} = 2(\cos x + \cos\alpha)\). Then \(\int 2(\cos x + \cos\alpha)\,dx = 2\sin x + 2x\cos\alpha + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{1 + \sin 2x}\).
solution: Note \(1 + \sin 2x = \sin^2 x + \cos^2 x + 2\sin x \cos x = (\sin x + \cos x)^2\). Put \(t = \sin x + \cos x\), so \(dt = (\cos x - \sin x)\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{1+\sin 2x}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{t^2} = -\frac{1}{t} + C = -\frac{1}{\sin x + \cos x} + C\).

Write \(\tan^3 2x \sec 2x = \tan^2 2x(\sec 2x \tan 2x) = (\sec^2 2x - 1)\sec 2x \tan 2x\). Put \(t = \sec 2x\), so \(dt = 2\sec 2x \tan 2x\,dx\). Then \(\int (\sec^2 2x - 1)\sec 2x \tan 2x\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int(t^2 - 1)\,dt = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{t^3}{3} - t\right) + C = \frac{\sec^3 2x}{6} - \frac{\sec 2x}{2} + C\).

\(\tan^4 x = \tan^2 x(\sec^2 x - 1) = \tan^2 x \sec^2 x - \tan^2 x = \tan^2 x \sec^2 x - (\sec^2 x - 1)\). Since \(\int \tan^2 x \sec^2 x\,dx = \frac{\tan^3 x}{3}\), \(\int \tan^4 x\,dx = \frac{\tan^3 x}{3} - \tan x + x + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x}\).
solution: Split the fraction: \(\frac{\sin^3 x + \cos^3 x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x} = \frac{\sin x}{\cos^2 x} + \frac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x} = \sec x \tan x + \csc x \cot x\). Then \(\int(\sec x \tan x + \csc x \cot x)\,dx = \sec x - \csc x + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{\cos 2x + 2\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x}\).
solution: Since \(\cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x\), the numerator \(\cos 2x + 2\sin^2 x = 1\). Hence \(\frac{\cos 2x + 2\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \frac{1}{\cos^2 x} = \sec^2 x\). Then \(\int \sec^2 x\,dx = \tan x + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{1}{\sin x \cos^3 x}\).
solution: Since \(\sin x \cos^3 x = \tan x \cos^4 x = \frac{\tan x}{\sec^4 x}\), we have \(\frac{1}{\sin x \cos^3 x} = \frac{\sec^4 x}{\tan x} = \frac{(1+\tan^2 x)\sec^2 x}{\tan x}\). Put \(t = \tan x\), \(dt = \sec^2 x\,dx\): \(\int \frac{1+t^2}{t}\,dt = \int\left(\frac{1}{t} + t\right)dt = \log|t| + \frac{t^2}{2} + C = \log|\tan x| + \frac{\tan^2 x}{2} + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{\cos 2x}{(\cos x + \sin x)^2}\).
solution: Since \(\cos 2x = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 x = (\cos x - \sin x)(\cos x + \sin x)\), \(\frac{\cos 2x}{(\cos x + \sin x)^2} = \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\). Put \(t = \cos x + \sin x\), so \(dt = (\cos x - \sin x)\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x - \sin x}{\cos x + \sin x}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log|t| + C = \log|\cos x + \sin x| + C\).

Write \(\cos x = \sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)\), so \(\sin^{-1}(\cos x) = \frac{\pi}{2} - x\) (taking the principal value, valid for \(0 \le x \le \pi\)). Then \(\int \sin^{-1}(\cos x)\,dx = \int\left(\frac{\pi}{2} - x\right)dx = \frac{\pi x}{2} - \frac{x^2}{2} + C\).

stem: Find the integral of \(\dfrac{1}{\cos (x - a) \cos (x - b)}\).
solution: Multiply and divide by \(\sin(a-b)\), and use \(\sin(a-b) = \sin\big[(x-b)-(x-a)\big]\). Since \(\frac{\sin[(x-b)-(x-a)]}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)} = \tan(x-b) - \tan(x-a)\), we get \(\frac{1}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)} = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\big[\tan(x-b) - \tan(x-a)\big]\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\cos(x-a)\cos(x-b)} = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\big[-\log|\cos(x-b)| + \log|\cos(x-a)|\big] + C = \frac{1}{\sin(a-b)}\log\left|\frac{\cos(x-a)}{\cos(x-b)}\right| + C\).

stem: \(\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sin^2 x - \cos^2 x}{\sin^2 x \cos^2 x}\,dx\) is equal to

solution:
(i) \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2-16} = \int \frac{dx}{x^2-4^2} = \frac{1}{8}\log\left|\frac{x-4}{x+4}\right| + C\) [by 7.4(1)].
(ii) \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{2x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1-(x-1)^2}}\). Put \(x-1=t\), so \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{2x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^2}} = \sin^{-1}(t) + C\) [by 7.4(5)] \(= \sin^{-1}(x-1) + C\).

(i) We have \(x^2-6x+13 = x^2-6x+3^2-3^2+13 = (x-3)^2+4\). So \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2-6x+13} = \int \frac{1}{(x-3)^2+2^2}\,dx\). Let \(x-3=t\), then \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2-6x+13} = \int \frac{dt}{t^2+2^2} = \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{t}{2} + C\) [by 7.4(3)] \(= \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x-3}{2} + C\).
(ii) The given integral is of the form 7.4(7). We write \(3x^2+13x-10 = 3\left(x^2+\frac{13x}{3}-\frac{10}{3}\right) = 3\left[\left(x+\frac{13}{6}\right)^2-\left(\frac{17}{6}\right)^2\right]\) (completing the square). Thus \(\int \frac{dx}{3x^2+13x-10} = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dx}{\left(x+\frac{13}{6}\right)^2-\left(\frac{17}{6}\right)^2}\). Put \(x+\frac{13}{6}=t\), then \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{3x^2+13x-10} = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{t^2-\left(\frac{17}{6}\right)^2} = \frac{1}{3\times 2\times \frac{17}{6}}\log\left|\frac{t-\frac{17}{6}}{t+\frac{17}{6}}\right| + C_1\) [by 7.4(1)] \(= \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{x+\frac{13}{6}-\frac{17}{6}}{x+\frac{13}{6}+\frac{17}{6}}\right| + C_1 = \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{6x-4}{6x+30}\right| + C_1 = \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{3x-2}{x+5}\right| + C_1 + \frac{1}{17}\log\frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{17}\log\left|\frac{3x-2}{x+5}\right| + C\), where \(C = C_1 + \frac{1}{17}\log\frac{1}{3}\).
(iii) We have \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5x^2-2x}} = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5\left(x^2-\frac{2x}{5}\right)}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{\left(x-\frac{1}{5}\right)^2-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}}\) (completing the square). Put \(x-\frac{1}{5}=t\), then \(dx=dt\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5x^2-2x}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2-\left(\frac{1}{5}\right)^2}\right| + C\) [by 7.4(4)] \(= \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}}\log\left|x-\frac{1}{5}+\sqrt{x^2-\frac{2x}{5}}\right| + C\).

(i) Using the formula 7.4(9), we express \(x+2 = A\frac{d}{dx}(2x^2+6x+5) + B = A(4x+6) + B\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant terms, \(4A=1\) and \(6A+B=2\), so \(A=\frac{1}{4}\) and \(B=\frac{1}{2}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x+2}{2x^2+6x+5}\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{4x+6}{2x^2+6x+5}\,dx + \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dx}{2x^2+6x+5} = \frac{1}{4}I_1 + \frac{1}{2}I_2\) ...(1). In \(I_1\), put \(2x^2+6x+5=t\), so \((4x+6)\,dx=dt\); thus \(I_1 = \int \frac{dt}{t} = \log|t| + C_1 = \log|2x^2+6x+5| + C_1\) ...(2). And \(I_2 = \int \frac{dx}{2x^2+6x+5} = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+3x+\frac{5}{2}} = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dx}{\left(x+\frac{3}{2}\right)^2+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2}\). Put \(x+\frac{3}{2}=t\), so \(dx=dt\): \(I_2 = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{t^2+\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2} = \frac{1}{2\times \frac{1}{2}}\tan^{-1}2t + C_2\) [by 7.4(3)] \(= \tan^{-1}2\left(x+\frac{3}{2}\right) + C_2 = \tan^{-1}(2x+3) + C_2\) ...(3). Using (2) and (3) in (1): \(\int \frac{x+2}{2x^2+6x+5}\,dx = \frac{1}{4}\log|2x^2+6x+5| + \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}(2x+3) + C\), where \(C = \frac{C_1}{4} + \frac{C_2}{2}\).
(ii) This integral is of the form given in 7.4(10). Express \(x+3 = A\frac{d}{dx}(5-4x-x^2) + B = A(-4-2x) + B\). Equating coefficients: \(-2A=1\) and \(-4A+B=3\), i.e. \(A=-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(B=1\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x+3}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}}\,dx = -\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{(-4-2x)\,dx}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}} + \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}} = -\frac{1}{2}I_1 + I_2\) ...(1). In \(I_1\), put \(5-4x-x^2=t\), so \((-4-2x)\,dx=dt\); thus \(I_1 = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t}} = 2\sqrt{t} + C_1 = 2\sqrt{5-4x-x^2} + C_1\) ...(2). Now \(I_2 = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{9-(x+2)^2}}\). Put \(x+2=t\), so \(dx=dt\): \(I_2 = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{3^2-t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\frac{t}{3} + C_2\) [by 7.4(5)] \(= \sin^{-1}\frac{x+2}{3} + C_2\) ...(3). Substituting (2) and (3) in (1): \(\int \frac{x+3}{\sqrt{5-4x-x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{5-4x-x^2} + \sin^{-1}\frac{x+2}{3} + C\), where \(C = C_2 - \frac{C_1}{2}\).
Put \(t = x^3\), so \(dt = 3x^2\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{3x^2}{x^6+1}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{t^2+1} = \tan^{-1} t + C = \tan^{-1}(x^3) + C\).

Write \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{1+4x^2}} = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{d(2x)}{\sqrt{1+(2x)^2}}\). Using \(\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2+a^2}} = \log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2+a^2}\right|\) with \(a=1\), this equals \(\frac{1}{2}\log\left|2x+\sqrt{1+4x^2}\right| + C\).
Put \(t = 2-x\), so \(dt = -dx\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{(2-x)^2+1}} = -\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2+1}} = -\log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2+1}\right| + C = -\log\left|(2-x)+\sqrt{x^2-4x+5}\right| + C\).

Write \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{9-25x^2}} = \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{d(5x)}{\sqrt{3^2-(5x)^2}}\). Using \(\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{a^2-t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\frac{t}{a}\) with \(a=3\), this equals \(\frac{1}{5}\sin^{-1}\frac{5x}{3} + C\).

Put \(t = x^2\), so \(dt = 2x\,dx\) and \(x\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}dt\). Then \(\int \frac{3x}{1+2x^4}\,dx = \frac{3}{2}\int \frac{dt}{1+2t^2} = \frac{3}{4}\int \frac{dt}{\tfrac{1}{2}+t^2} = \frac{3}{4}\cdot\sqrt{2}\,\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{2}\,t) + C = \frac{3}{2\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{2}\,x^2) + C\).

Put \(t = x^3\), so \(dt = 3x^2\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{x^2}{1-x^6}\,dx = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{1-t^2} = \frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\log\left|\frac{1+t}{1-t}\right| + C = \frac{1}{6}\log\left|\frac{1+x^3}{1-x^3}\right| + C\).

Split as \(\int \frac{x-1}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\,dx = \int \frac{x}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\,dx - \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\). For the first, put \(u=x^2-1\), giving \(\sqrt{x^2-1}\); the second is \(\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right|\). Hence the integral \(= \sqrt{x^2-1} - \log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right| + C\).

Put \(t = x^3\), so \(dt = 3x^2\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{x^2}{\sqrt{x^6+a^6}}\,dx = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2+(a^3)^2}} = \frac{1}{3}\log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2+a^6}\right| + C = \frac{1}{3}\log\left|x^3+\sqrt{x^6+a^6}\right| + C\).

Put \(t = \tan x\), so \(dt = \sec^2 x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\sec^2 x}{\sqrt{\tan^2 x+4}}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2+2^2}} = \log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2+4}\right| + C = \log\left|\tan x+\sqrt{\tan^2 x+4}\right| + C\).

Complete the square: \(x^2+2x+2 = (x+1)^2+1\). Put \(t=x+1\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2+2x+2}} = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2+1}} = \log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2+1}\right| + C = \log\left|(x+1)+\sqrt{x^2+2x+2}\right| + C\).

Complete the square: \(9x^2+6x+5 = (3x+1)^2+4\). Put \(t=3x+1\), \(dt=3\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{9x^2+6x+5} = \frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dt}{t^2+2^2} = \frac{1}{3}\cdot\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{t}{2} + C = \frac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3x+1}{2}\right) + C\).
Rewrite \(7-6x-x^2 = 16-(x+3)^2\). Put \(t=x+3\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{7-6x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{4^2-t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\frac{t}{4} + C = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x+3}{4}\right) + C\).

Expand and complete the square: \((x-1)(x-2) = x^2-3x+2 = \left(x-\tfrac{3}{2}\right)^2-\tfrac{1}{4}\). Put \(t=x-\tfrac{3}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{(x-1)(x-2)}} = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2-(1/2)^2}} = \log\left|t+\sqrt{t^2-\tfrac{1}{4}}\right| + C = \log\left|\left(x-\tfrac{3}{2}\right)+\sqrt{x^2-3x+2}\right| + C\).

Rewrite \(8+3x-x^2 = \tfrac{41}{4}-\left(x-\tfrac{3}{2}\right)^2\). Put \(t=x-\tfrac{3}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{8+3x-x^2}} = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{\left(\tfrac{\sqrt{41}}{2}\right)^2-t^2}} = \sin^{-1}\frac{t}{\sqrt{41}/2} + C = \sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2x-3}{\sqrt{41}}\right) + C\).

Expand and complete the square: \((x-a)(x-b) = \left(x-\tfrac{a+b}{2}\right)^2-\left(\tfrac{a-b}{2}\right)^2\). Put \(t=x-\tfrac{a+b}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{(x-a)(x-b)}} = \int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t^2-\left(\tfrac{a-b}{2}\right)^2}} = \log\left|\left(x-\tfrac{a+b}{2}\right)+\sqrt{(x-a)(x-b)}\right| + C\).

The numerator is exactly the derivative of the quantity under the root: \(\frac{d}{dx}(2x^2+x-3) = 4x+1\). Put \(u=2x^2+x-3\), so \(du=(4x+1)\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{4x+1}{\sqrt{2x^2+x-3}}\,dx = \int \frac{du}{\sqrt{u}} = 2\sqrt{u} + C = 2\sqrt{2x^2+x-3} + C\).

Write \(x+2 = \tfrac{1}{2}(2x)+2\), so \(\int \frac{x+2}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\,dx + 2\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2-1}}\). The first term gives \(\sqrt{x^2-1}\) and the second \(2\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right|\). Hence the integral \(= \sqrt{x^2-1} + 2\log\left|x+\sqrt{x^2-1}\right| + C\).

Denominator \(3x^2+2x+1\) has derivative \(6x+2\). Write \(5x-2 = \tfrac{5}{6}(6x+2)-\tfrac{11}{3}\). Then \(\int \frac{5x-2}{3x^2+2x+1}\,dx = \frac{5}{6}\log\left|3x^2+2x+1\right| - \frac{11}{3}\int \frac{dx}{3x^2+2x+1}\). Since \(3x^2+2x+1 = 3\left[\left(x+\tfrac{1}{3}\right)^2+\tfrac{2}{9}\right]\), \(\int \frac{dx}{3x^2+2x+1} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3x+1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\). Hence the integral \(= \frac{5}{6}\log\left|3x^2+2x+1\right| - \frac{11}{3\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3x+1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + C\).

Here \((x-5)(x-4) = x^2-9x+20\), whose derivative is \(2x-9\). Write \(6x+7 = 3(2x-9)+34\). Then \(\int \frac{6x+7}{\sqrt{x^2-9x+20}}\,dx = 3\int \frac{2x-9}{\sqrt{x^2-9x+20}}\,dx + 34\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{x^2-9x+20}}\). The first term is \(6\sqrt{x^2-9x+20}\); since \(x^2-9x+20 = \left(x-\tfrac{9}{2}\right)^2-\tfrac{1}{4}\), the second is \(34\log\left|\left(x-\tfrac{9}{2}\right)+\sqrt{x^2-9x+20}\right|\). Hence \(= 6\sqrt{x^2-9x+20} + 34\log\left|\left(x-\tfrac{9}{2}\right)+\sqrt{x^2-9x+20}\right| + C\).

Note \(\frac{d}{dx}(4x-x^2) = 4-2x\) and \(4x-x^2 = 4-(x-2)^2\). Write \(x+2 = -\tfrac{1}{2}(4-2x)+4\). Then \(\int \frac{x+2}{\sqrt{4x-x^2}}\,dx = -\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{4-2x}{\sqrt{4x-x^2}}\,dx + 4\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{4-(x-2)^2}}\). The first term is \(-\sqrt{4x-x^2}\) and the second \(4\sin^{-1}\frac{x-2}{2}\). Hence the integral \(= -\sqrt{4x-x^2} + 4\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x-2}{2}\right) + C\).

Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^2+2x+3) = 2x+2\), write \(x+2 = \tfrac{1}{2}(2x+2)+1\). Then \(\int \frac{x+2}{\sqrt{x^2+2x+3}}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2x+2}{\sqrt{x^2+2x+3}}\,dx + \int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{(x+1)^2+2}}\). The first term is \(\sqrt{x^2+2x+3}\) and the second \(\log\left|(x+1)+\sqrt{x^2+2x+3}\right|\). Hence \(= \sqrt{x^2+2x+3} + \log\left|(x+1)+\sqrt{x^2+2x+3}\right| + C\).

Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^2-2x-5) = 2x-2\), write \(x+3 = \tfrac{1}{2}(2x-2)+4\). Then \(\int \frac{x+3}{x^2-2x-5}\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\log\left|x^2-2x-5\right| + 4\int \frac{dx}{(x-1)^2-6}\). Using \(\int \frac{dt}{t^2-a^2} = \frac{1}{2a}\log\left|\frac{t-a}{t+a}\right|\) with \(t=x-1,\ a=\sqrt{6}\), the second term is \(\frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\log\left|\frac{x-1-\sqrt{6}}{x-1+\sqrt{6}}\right|\). Hence \(= \frac{1}{2}\log\left|x^2-2x-5\right| + \frac{2}{\sqrt{6}}\log\left|\frac{x-1-\sqrt{6}}{x-1+\sqrt{6}}\right| + C\).

Since \(\frac{d}{dx}(x^2+4x+10) = 2x+4\), write \(5x+3 = \tfrac{5}{2}(2x+4)-7\). Then \(\int \frac{5x+3}{\sqrt{x^2+4x+10}}\,dx = \frac{5}{2}\int \frac{2x+4}{\sqrt{x^2+4x+10}}\,dx - 7\int \frac{dx}{\sqrt{(x+2)^2+6}}\). The first term is \(5\sqrt{x^2+4x+10}\) and the second \(-7\log\left|(x+2)+\sqrt{x^2+4x+10}\right|\). Hence \(= 5\sqrt{x^2+4x+10} - 7\log\left|(x+2)+\sqrt{x^2+4x+10}\right| + C\).

The integrand is a proper rational function. By the form of partial fraction [Table 7.2 (i)], write \(\frac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \frac{A}{x+1} + \frac{B}{x+2}\). This gives \(1 = A(x+2) + B(x+1)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and the constant term, \(A+B=0\) and \(2A+B=1\), so \(A=1\) and \(B=-1\). Thus \(\frac{1}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \frac{1}{x+1} - \frac{1}{x+2}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{dx}{(x+1)(x+2)} = \int \frac{dx}{x+1} - \int \frac{dx}{x+2} = \log|x+1| - \log|x+2| + C = \log\left|\frac{x+1}{x+2}\right| + C\).

Here the integrand \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6}\) is not a proper rational function, so we divide \(x^2+1\) by \(x^2-5x+6\) and find that \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 + \frac{5x-5}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 + \frac{5x-5}{(x-2)(x-3)}\). Let \(\frac{5x-5}{(x-2)(x-3)} = \frac{A}{x-2} + \frac{B}{x-3}\), so that \(5x-5 = A(x-3) + B(x-2)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x\) and constant terms, \(A+B=5\) and \(3A+2B=5\), giving \(A=-5\) and \(B=10\). Thus \(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6} = 1 - \frac{5}{x-2} + \frac{10}{x-3}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2+1}{x^2-5x+6}\,dx = \int dx - 5\int \frac{1}{x-2}\,dx + 10\int \frac{dx}{x-3} = x - 5\log|x-2| + 10\log|x-3| + C\).

The integrand is of the type as given in Table 7.2 (4). Write \(\frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)} = \frac{A}{x+1} + \frac{B}{(x+1)^2} + \frac{C}{x+3}\), so that \(3x-2 = A(x+1)(x+3) + B(x+3) + C(x+1)^2 = A(x^2+4x+3) + B(x+3) + C(x^2+2x+1)\). Comparing the coefficient of \(x^2\), \(x\) and the constant term on both sides, \(A+C=0\), \(4A+B+2C=3\) and \(3A+3B+C=-2\). Solving these, \(A=\frac{11}{4}\), \(B=\frac{-5}{2}\) and \(C=\frac{-11}{4}\). Thus the integrand is \(\frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)} = \frac{11}{4(x+1)} - \frac{5}{2(x+1)^2} - \frac{11}{4(x+3)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{3x-2}{(x+1)^2(x+3)}\,dx = \frac{11}{4}\int \frac{dx}{x+1} - \frac{5}{2}\int \frac{dx}{(x+1)^2} - \frac{11}{4}\int \frac{dx}{x+3} = \frac{11}{4}\log|x+1| + \frac{5}{2(x+1)} - \frac{11}{4}\log|x+3| + C = \frac{11}{4}\log\left|\frac{x+1}{x+3}\right| + \frac{5}{2(x+1)} + C\).

Consider \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)}\) and put \(x^2=y\). Then \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = \frac{y}{(y+1)(y+4)}\). Write \(\frac{y}{(y+1)(y+4)} = \frac{A}{y+1} + \frac{B}{y+4}\), so that \(y = A(y+4) + B(y+1)\). Comparing coefficients of \(y\) and constant terms, \(A+B=1\) and \(4A+B=0\), which give \(A=-\frac{1}{3}\) and \(B=\frac{4}{3}\). Thus \(\frac{x^2}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = -\frac{1}{3(x^2+1)} + \frac{4}{3(x^2+4)}\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2\,dx}{(x^2+1)(x^2+4)} = -\frac{1}{3}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+1} + \frac{4}{3}\int \frac{dx}{x^2+4} = -\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}x + \frac{4}{3}\times\frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C = -\frac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}x + \frac{2}{3}\tan^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C\). Here the substitution was made only for the partial fraction part and not for the integration part.

Let \(y=\sin\phi\). Then \(dy=\cos\phi\,d\phi\). Therefore \(\int \frac{(3\sin\phi-2)\cos\phi}{5-\cos^2\phi-4\sin\phi}\,d\phi = \int \frac{(3y-2)\,dy}{5-(1-y^2)-4y} = \int \frac{3y-2}{y^2-4y+4}\,dy = \int \frac{3y-2}{(y-2)^2}\,dy = I\) (say). Now write \(\frac{3y-2}{(y-2)^2} = \frac{A}{y-2} + \frac{B}{(y-2)^2}\) [by Table 7.2 (2)], so that \(3y-2 = A(y-2) + B\). Comparing the coefficients of \(y\) and constant term, \(A=3\) and \(B-2A=-2\), which give \(A=3\) and \(B=4\). Therefore \(I = \int \left[\frac{3}{y-2} + \frac{4}{(y-2)^2}\right]dy = 3\int \frac{dy}{y-2} + 4\int \frac{dy}{(y-2)^2} = 3\log|y-2| + 4\left(-\frac{1}{y-2}\right) + C = 3\log|\sin\phi-2| + \frac{4}{2-\sin\phi} + C = 3\log(2-\sin\phi) + \frac{4}{2-\sin\phi} + C\) (since \(2-\sin\phi\) is always positive).

The integrand is a proper rational function. Decompose it into partial fractions [Table 7.2 (5)]. Write \(\frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)} = \frac{A}{x+2} + \frac{Bx+C}{x^2+1}\). Therefore \(x^2+x+1 = A(x^2+1) + (Bx+C)(x+2)\). Equating the coefficients of \(x^2\), \(x\) and the constant term of both sides, \(A+B=1\), \(2B+C=1\) and \(A+2C=1\). Solving these, \(A=\frac{3}{5}\), \(B=\frac{2}{5}\) and \(C=\frac{1}{5}\). Thus the integrand is \(\frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)} = \frac{3}{5(x+2)} + \frac{1}{5}\left(\frac{2x+1}{x^2+1}\right)\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^2+x+1}{(x^2+1)(x+2)}\,dx = \frac{3}{5}\int \frac{dx}{x+2} + \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{2x}{x^2+1}\,dx + \frac{1}{5}\int \frac{1}{x^2+1}\,dx = \frac{3}{5}\log|x+2| + \frac{1}{5}\log|x^2+1| + \frac{1}{5}\tan^{-1}x + C\).

Here \(\frac{1}{x^2-9} = \frac{1}{(x-3)(x+3)} = \frac{1}{6}\left(\frac{1}{x-3} - \frac{1}{x+3}\right)\). Hence \(\int \frac{dx}{x^2-9} = \frac{1}{6}\big(\log|x-3| - \log|x+3|\big) + C = \frac{1}{6}\log\left|\frac{x-3}{x+3}\right| + C\).

The fraction is improper; dividing, \(\frac{1-x^2}{x(1-2x)} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1-\frac{x}{2}}{x(1-2x)}\). Write \(\frac{1-\frac{x}{2}}{x(1-2x)} = \frac{A}{x} + \frac{B}{1-2x}\), so \(1-\tfrac{x}{2} = A(1-2x)+Bx\). Put \(x=0\): \(A=1\); \(x=\tfrac{1}{2}\): \(\tfrac{3}{4}=\tfrac{B}{2}\Rightarrow B=\tfrac{3}{2}\). Hence \(\int \frac{1-x^2}{x(1-2x)}\,dx = \int\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{x} + \frac{3}{2(1-2x)}\right)dx = \frac{x}{2} + \log|x| - \frac{3}{4}\log|1-2x| + C\).

Let \(\frac{x}{(x^2+1)(x-1)} = \frac{Ax+B}{x^2+1} + \frac{C}{x-1}\), so \(x = (Ax+B)(x-1) + C(x^2+1)\). Put \(x=1\): \(1=2C\Rightarrow C=\tfrac{1}{2}\); comparing \(x^2\): \(A+C=0\Rightarrow A=-\tfrac{1}{2}\); comparing \(x\): \(B-A=1\Rightarrow B=\tfrac{1}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{x}{(x^2+1)(x-1)}\,dx = \int\left(\frac{-\tfrac{1}{2}x+\tfrac{1}{2}}{x^2+1} + \frac{\tfrac{1}{2}}{x-1}\right)dx = -\frac{1}{4}\log(x^2+1) + \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x + \frac{1}{2}\log|x-1| + C\).

Let \(\frac{x}{(x-1)^2(x+2)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{(x-1)^2} + \frac{C}{x+2}\), so \(x = A(x-1)(x+2) + B(x+2) + C(x-1)^2\). Put \(x=1\): \(1=3B\Rightarrow B=\tfrac{1}{3}\); \(x=-2\): \(-2=9C\Rightarrow C=-\tfrac{2}{9}\); comparing \(x^2\): \(A+C=0\Rightarrow A=\tfrac{2}{9}\). Then \(\int \frac{x}{(x-1)^2(x+2)}\,dx = \frac{2}{9}\log|x-1| - \frac{1}{3(x-1)} - \frac{2}{9}\log|x+2| + C\).

The fraction is improper; dividing, \(\frac{x^3+x+1}{x^2-1} = x + \frac{2x+1}{x^2-1}\). Write \(\frac{2x+1}{(x-1)(x+1)} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{x+1}\), so \(2x+1 = A(x+1)+B(x-1)\). Put \(x=1\): \(3=2A\Rightarrow A=\tfrac{3}{2}\); \(x=-1\): \(-1=-2B\Rightarrow B=\tfrac{1}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{x^3+x+1}{x^2-1}\,dx = \frac{x^2}{2} + \frac{3}{2}\log|x-1| + \frac{1}{2}\log|x+1| + C\).

Let \(\frac{2}{(1-x)(1+x^2)} = \frac{A}{1-x} + \frac{Bx+C}{1+x^2}\), so \(2 = A(1+x^2) + (Bx+C)(1-x)\). Put \(x=1\): \(2=2A\Rightarrow A=1\); comparing \(x^2\): \(A-B=0\Rightarrow B=1\); comparing \(x\): \(B-C=0\Rightarrow C=1\). Then \(\int \frac{2}{(1-x)(1+x^2)}\,dx = \int\left(\frac{1}{1-x} + \frac{x+1}{1+x^2}\right)dx = -\log|1-x| + \frac{1}{2}\log(1+x^2) + \tan^{-1}x + C\).

Put \(t = x+2\), so \(dt=dx\) and \(3x-1 = 3t-7\). Then \(\int \frac{3x-1}{(x+2)^2}\,dx = \int \frac{3t-7}{t^2}\,dt = \int\left(\frac{3}{t} - \frac{7}{t^2}\right)dt = 3\log|t| + \frac{7}{t} + C = 3\log|x+2| + \frac{7}{x+2} + C\).

Factor \(x^4-1=(x-1)(x+1)(x^2+1)\). Let \(\frac{1}{x^4-1} = \frac{A}{x-1} + \frac{B}{x+1} + \frac{Cx+D}{x^2+1}\), so \(1 = A(x+1)(x^2+1) + B(x-1)(x^2+1) + (Cx+D)(x^2-1)\). Put \(x=1\): \(A=\tfrac{1}{4}\); \(x=-1\): \(B=-\tfrac{1}{4}\); comparing \(x^3\): \(A+B+C=0\Rightarrow C=0\); constant: \(A-B-D=1\Rightarrow D=-\tfrac{1}{2}\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{x^4-1} = \frac{1}{4}\log|x-1| - \frac{1}{4}\log|x+1| - \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x + C = \frac{1}{4}\log\left|\frac{x-1}{x+1}\right| - \frac{1}{2}\tan^{-1}x + C\).

stem: Integrate the rational function \(\frac{1}{x(x^n+1)}\). [Hint: multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^{n-1}\) and put \(x^n=t\)]
solution: Multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^{n-1}\): \(\frac{1}{x(x^n+1)} = \frac{x^{n-1}}{x^n(x^n+1)}\). Put \(t = x^n\), so \(dt = n\,x^{n-1}\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{x(x^n+1)} = \frac{1}{n}\int \frac{dt}{t(t+1)} = \frac{1}{n}\int\left(\frac{1}{t} - \frac{1}{t+1}\right)dt = \frac{1}{n}\log\left|\frac{t}{t+1}\right| + C = \frac{1}{n}\log\left|\frac{x^n}{x^n+1}\right| + C\).

stem: Integrate the rational function \(\frac{\cos x}{(1-\sin x)(2-\sin x)}\). [Hint: Put \(\sin x=t\)]
solution: Put \(t = \sin x\), so \(dt = \cos x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{\cos x}{(1-\sin x)(2-\sin x)}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{(1-t)(2-t)}\). Since \(\frac{1}{(1-t)(2-t)} = \frac{1}{1-t} - \frac{1}{2-t}\), this equals \(-\log|1-t| + \log|2-t| + C = \log\left|\frac{2-\sin x}{1-\sin x}\right| + C\).

Put \(t = x^2\), so \(dt = 2x\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{2x}{(x^2+1)(x^2+3)}\,dx = \int \frac{dt}{(t+1)(t+3)}\). Since \(\frac{1}{(t+1)(t+3)} = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{t+1} - \frac{1}{t+3}\right)\), this equals \(\frac{1}{2}\log\left|\frac{t+1}{t+3}\right| + C = \frac{1}{2}\log\left(\frac{x^2+1}{x^2+3}\right) + C\).

Multiply numerator and denominator by \(x^3\): \(\frac{1}{x(x^4-1)} = \frac{x^3}{x^4(x^4-1)}\). Put \(t = x^4\), so \(dt = 4x^3\,dx\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{x(x^4-1)} = \frac{1}{4}\int \frac{dt}{t(t-1)} = \frac{1}{4}\int\left(\frac{1}{t-1} - \frac{1}{t}\right)dt = \frac{1}{4}\log\left|\frac{t-1}{t}\right| + C = \frac{1}{4}\log\left|\frac{x^4-1}{x^4}\right| + C\).

Put \(t = e^x\), so \(dt = e^x\,dx\) and \(dx = \frac{dt}{t}\). Then \(\int \frac{dx}{e^x-1} = \int \frac{dt}{t(t-1)} = \int\left(\frac{1}{t-1} - \frac{1}{t}\right)dt = \log|t-1| - \log|t| + C = \log\left|\frac{e^x-1}{e^x}\right| + C = \log|e^x-1| - x + C\).

Put \(f(x) = x\) (first function) and \(g(x) = \cos x\) (second function). Then, integration by parts gives \(\int x \cos x \, dx = x \int \cos x \, dx - \int [\frac{d}{dx}(x) \int \cos x \, dx]\, dx = x \sin x - \int \sin x \, dx = x \sin x + \cos x + C\). Note the choice of first and second function matters: taking \(f(x) = \cos x\) and \(g(x) = x\) instead reduces the integral to the more complicated \(\int \sin x \, \frac{x^2}{2}\, dx\).

We cannot guess a function whose derivative is \(\log x\). Take \(\log x\) as the first function and the constant function \(1\) as the second function; the integral of the second function is \(x\). Hence \(\int (\log x \cdot 1)\, dx = \log x \int 1\, dx - \int [\frac{d}{dx}(\log x) \int 1\, dx]\, dx = (\log x)\cdot x - \int \frac{1}{x}\, x \, dx = x \log x - x + C\).

Take the first function as \(x\) and the second function as \(e^{x}\). The integral of the second function is \(e^{x}\). Therefore \(\int x\, e^{x} \, dx = x\, e^{x} - \int 1 \cdot e^{x} \, dx = x e^{x} - e^{x} + C\).

Let the first function be \(\sin^{-1} x\) and the second function be \(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\). First find the integral of the second function \(\int \frac{x\, dx}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\): put \(t = 1 - x^{2}\), then \(dt = -2x\, dx\), so \(\int \frac{x\, dx}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}} = -\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{dt}{\sqrt{t}} = -\sqrt{t} = -\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\). Hence \(\int \frac{x \sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}\, dx = (\sin^{-1} x)(-\sqrt{1-x^{2}}) - \int \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^{2}}}(-\sqrt{1-x^{2}})\, dx = -\sqrt{1-x^{2}}\,\sin^{-1} x + x + C = x - \sqrt{1-x^{2}}\,\sin^{-1} x + C\). (Alternatively, substitute \(\sin^{-1} x = \theta\) and then integrate by parts.)

Take \(e^{x}\) as the first function and \(\sin x\) as the second function. Integrating by parts, \(I = \int e^{x} \sin x \, dx = e^{x}(-\cos x) + \int e^{x} \cos x \, dx = -e^{x}\cos x + I_1\) (say) ...(1). Taking \(e^{x}\) and \(\cos x\) as the first and second functions in \(I_1\), we get \(I_1 = e^{x} \sin x - \int e^{x} \sin x \, dx\). Substituting \(I_1\) in (1): \(I = -e^{x}\cos x + e^{x}\sin x - I\), or \(2I = e^{x}(\sin x - \cos x)\). Hence \(I = \int e^{x} \sin x \, dx = \frac{e^{x}}{2}(\sin x - \cos x) + C\).

We have \(I = \int e^{x}\left(\tan^{-1} x + \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\right) dx\). Consider \(f(x) = \tan^{-1} x\), then \(f'(x) = \frac{1}{1+x^{2}}\). Thus the integrand is of the form \(e^{x}[f(x) + f'(x)]\), and \(\int e^{x}[f(x)+f'(x)]\, dx = e^{x} f(x) + C\). Therefore \(I = e^{x} \tan^{-1} x + C\).

We have \(I = \int \frac{(x^{2}+1)\, e^{x}}{(x+1)^{2}}\, dx = \int e^{x}\left[\frac{x^{2}-1+1+1}{(x+1)^{2}}\right] dx = \int e^{x}\left[\frac{x^{2}-1}{(x+1)^{2}} + \frac{2}{(x+1)^{2}}\right] dx = \int e^{x}\left[\frac{x-1}{x+1} + \frac{2}{(x+1)^{2}}\right] dx\). Consider \(f(x) = \frac{x-1}{x+1}\), then \(f'(x) = \frac{2}{(x+1)^{2}}\). Thus the integrand is of the form \(e^{x}[f(x) + f'(x)]\). Therefore \(\int \frac{x^{2}+1}{(x+1)^{2}}\, e^{x} \, dx = \frac{x-1}{x+1}\, e^{x} + C\).
By parts with \(u = x\), \(dv = \sin x\,dx\), so \(du = dx\), \(v = -\cos x\). Then \(\int x \sin x\,dx = -x\cos x + \int \cos x\,dx = -x\cos x + \sin x + C\).

By parts with \(u = x\), \(dv = \sin 3x\,dx\), so \(v = -\tfrac{1}{3}\cos 3x\). Then \(\int x \sin 3x\,dx = -\tfrac{x}{3}\cos 3x + \tfrac{1}{3}\int \cos 3x\,dx = -\tfrac{x}{3}\cos 3x + \tfrac{1}{9}\sin 3x + C\).

By parts with \(u = x^2\), \(dv = e^x\,dx\): \(\int x^2 e^x\,dx = x^2 e^x - 2\int x e^x\,dx\). Since \(\int x e^x\,dx = x e^x - e^x\), we get \(\int x^2 e^x\,dx = x^2 e^x - 2(x e^x - e^x) = e^x(x^2 - 2x + 2) + C\).

Take \(u = \log x\) (ILATE), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \log x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \int \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \tfrac{1}{2}\int x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \tfrac{x^2}{4} + C\).

Take \(u = \log 2x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(du = \tfrac{1}{x}\,dx\), \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \log 2x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log 2x - \int \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cdot\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log 2x - \tfrac{x^2}{4} + C\).

Take \(u = \log x\), \(dv = x^2\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\). Then \(\int x^2 \log x\,dx = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \int \tfrac{x^3}{3}\cdot\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \tfrac{1}{3}\int x^2\,dx = \tfrac{x^3}{3}\log x - \tfrac{x^3}{9} + C\).

Take \(u = \sin^{-1} x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \sin^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\sin^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Writing \(x^2 = 1-(1-x^2)\), \(\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = \sin^{-1} x - \int \sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx = \sin^{-1} x - \big(\tfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1-x^2} + \tfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1} x\big)\). Hence \(\int x \sin^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{2x^2-1}{4}\sin^{-1} x + \tfrac{x}{4}\sqrt{1-x^2} + C\).

Take \(u = \tan^{-1} x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\). Then \(\int x \tan^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\int \tfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx\). Since \(\int \tfrac{x^2}{1+x^2}\,dx = \int\big(1 - \tfrac{1}{1+x^2}\big)dx = x - \tan^{-1} x\), we get \(\int x \tan^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}(x^2+1)\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{x}{2} + C\).

Take \(u = \cos^{-1} x\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\), \(du = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Then \(\int x \cos^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cos^{-1} x + \tfrac{1}{2}\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Using \(\int \tfrac{x^2}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = \tfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1} x - \tfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1-x^2}\), we get \(\int x \cos^{-1} x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\cos^{-1} x + \tfrac{1}{4}\sin^{-1} x - \tfrac{x}{4}\sqrt{1-x^2} + C\).

Take \(u = (\sin^{-1} x)^2\), \(dv = dx\), \(v = x\): \(\int (\sin^{-1} x)^2\,dx = x(\sin^{-1} x)^2 - 2\int \tfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). For the remaining integral take \(u = \sin^{-1} x\), \(dv = \tfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\), \(v = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\): \(\int \tfrac{x\sin^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\sin^{-1} x + \int 1\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\sin^{-1} x + x\). Therefore \(\int (\sin^{-1} x)^2\,dx = x(\sin^{-1} x)^2 + 2\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\sin^{-1} x - 2x + C\).

Take \(u = \cos^{-1} x\), \(dv = \tfrac{x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\), so \(v = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\) and \(du = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx\). Then \(\int \tfrac{x\cos^{-1} x}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\cos^{-1} x - \int \big(-\sqrt{1-x^2}\big)\big(-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{1-x^2}}\big)dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\cos^{-1} x - \int 1\,dx = -\sqrt{1-x^2}\,\cos^{-1} x - x + C\).
Take \(u = x\), \(dv = \sec^2 x\,dx\), so \(v = \tan x\). Then \(\int x \sec^2 x\,dx = x\tan x - \int \tan x\,dx = x\tan x - (-\log|\cos x|) = x\tan x + \log|\cos x| + C\).

Write \(\tan^{-1} x = 1\cdot\tan^{-1} x\) and take \(u = \tan^{-1} x\), \(dv = dx\), \(v = x\). Then \(\int \tan^{-1} x\,dx = x\tan^{-1} x - \int \tfrac{x}{1+x^2}\,dx = x\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\log(1+x^2) + C\).

Take \(u = (\log x)^2\), \(dv = x\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\), \(du = \tfrac{2\log x}{x}\,dx\). Then \(\int x(\log x)^2\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}(\log x)^2 - \int x \log x\,dx\). Using \(\int x \log x\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x - \tfrac{x^2}{4}\), we get \(\int x(\log x)^2\,dx = \tfrac{x^2}{2}(\log x)^2 - \tfrac{x^2}{2}\log x + \tfrac{x^2}{4} + C\).

Take \(u = \log x\), \(dv = (x^2+1)\,dx\), so \(v = \tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\). Then \(\int (x^2+1)\log x\,dx = \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\log x - \int \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\tfrac{1}{x}\,dx = \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\log x - \int \big(\tfrac{x^2}{3} + 1\big)dx = \big(\tfrac{x^3}{3} + x\big)\log x - \tfrac{x^3}{9} - x + C\).
This has the form \(\int e^x\big[f(x) + f'(x)\big]dx = e^x f(x) + C\) with \(f(x) = \sin x\), \(f'(x) = \cos x\). Hence \(\int e^x(\sin x + \cos x)\,dx = e^x \sin x + C\).

Write \(\tfrac{x}{(1+x)^2} = \tfrac{(1+x)-1}{(1+x)^2} = \tfrac{1}{1+x} - \tfrac{1}{(1+x)^2}\), so the integrand is \(e^x\big[f(x)+f'(x)\big]\) with \(f(x) = \tfrac{1}{1+x}\), \(f'(x) = -\tfrac{1}{(1+x)^2}\). Hence \(\int \tfrac{x e^x}{(1+x)^2}\,dx = \tfrac{e^x}{1+x} + C\).

Using \(1+\cos x = 2\cos^2\tfrac{x}{2}\) and \(1+\sin x = 1 + 2\sin\tfrac{x}{2}\cos\tfrac{x}{2}\), \(\tfrac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x} = \tfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\tfrac{x}{2} + \tan\tfrac{x}{2}\). So the integrand is \(e^x\big[f(x)+f'(x)\big]\) with \(f(x) = \tan\tfrac{x}{2}\), \(f'(x) = \tfrac{1}{2}\sec^2\tfrac{x}{2}\). Hence \(\int e^x\Big(\tfrac{1+\sin x}{1+\cos x}\Big)dx = e^x \tan\tfrac{x}{2} + C\).
This is \(\int e^x\big[f(x) + f'(x)\big]dx\) with \(f(x) = \tfrac{1}{x}\), \(f'(x) = -\tfrac{1}{x^2}\). Hence \(\int e^x\big(\tfrac{1}{x} - \tfrac{1}{x^2}\big)dx = \tfrac{e^x}{x} + C\).
Using \(\int e^{ax}\sin bx\,dx = \tfrac{e^{ax}}{a^2+b^2}(a\sin bx - b\cos bx) + C\) with \(a = 2\), \(b = 1\): \(\int e^{2x}\sin x\,dx = \tfrac{e^{2x}}{5}(2\sin x - \cos x) + C\).

Put \(x = \tan\theta\), so \(\tfrac{2x}{1+x^2} = \sin 2\theta\) and \(\sin^{-1}\big(\tfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\big) = 2\theta = 2\tan^{-1} x\) (for \(-1\le x\le 1\)). Then \(\int \sin^{-1}\big(\tfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\big)dx = 2\int \tan^{-1} x\,dx = 2\big(x\tan^{-1} x - \tfrac{1}{2}\log(1+x^2)\big) = 2x\tan^{-1} x - \log(1+x^2) + C\).

Note that \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5}\,dx = \int \sqrt{(x+1)^2 + 4}\,dx\). Put \(x + 1 = y\), so that \(dx = dy\). Then \(\int \sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5}\,dx = \int \sqrt{y^2 + 2^2}\,dy = \frac{1}{2}\,y\sqrt{y^2 + 4} + \frac{4}{2}\log\left|\,y + \sqrt{y^2 + 4}\,\right| + C\) [using 7.6.2 (ii)] \(= \frac{1}{2}(x+1)\sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5} + 2\log\left|\,x + 1 + \sqrt{x^2 + 2x + 5}\,\right| + C\).

Note that \(\int \sqrt{3 - 2x - x^2}\,dx = \int \sqrt{4 - (x+1)^2}\,dx\). Put \(x + 1 = y\) so that \(dx = dy\). Thus \(\int \sqrt{3 - 2x - x^2}\,dx = \int \sqrt{4 - y^2}\,dy = \frac{1}{2}\,y\sqrt{4 - y^2} + \frac{4}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{y}{2} + C\) [using 7.6.2 (iii)] \(= \frac{1}{2}(x+1)\sqrt{3 - 2x - x^2} + 2\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{x+1}{2}\right) + C\).

Use \(\int \sqrt{a^2 - x^2}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} + \frac{a^2}{2}\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{a} + C\) with \(a = 2\). So \(\int \sqrt{4 - x^2}\,dx = \frac{x}{2}\sqrt{4 - x^2} + 2\sin^{-1}\frac{x}{2} + C\).
